Positive counts are P1 (ivory) checkers, negative counts P2 (obsidian). P1 moves\n * from 24 toward 1; P2's point {@code q} is P1's point {@code 25 - q}.\n *\n * @param phase   OPENING (one roll decides who starts), ROLL (the side to move must roll) or MOVE\n *                (the side to move must play {@code dice})\n * @param dice    the current or most recent roll, two values; doubles are played four times\n * @param opening the opening roll as [P1's die, P2's die] until the next roll; null otherwise\n * @param notices turns passed automatically since the last action (no legal moves, closed out)\n * @param lastTurn the most recent turn played, for highlighting; null if none yet\n */\npublic record BackgammonState(\n        List<Integer> points,\n        int barP1,\n        int barP2,\n        int offP1,\n        int offP2,\n        Side sideToMove,\n        Phase phase,\n        List<Integer> dice,\n        List<Integer> opening,\n        List<Notice> notices,\n        BackgammonMove lastTurn) {\n\n    public static final int CHECKERS = 15;\n\n    public BackgammonState {\n        if (points.size() != 24) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"A backgammon board has 24 points\");\n        }\n        points = List.copyOf(points);\n        dice = dice == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(dice);\n        notices = notices == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(notices);\n    }\n\n    public enum Phase {\n        OPENING,\n        ROLL,\n        MOVE\n    }\n\n    public enum NoticeKind {\n        NO_MOVES,\n        CLOSED_OUT\n    }\n\n    /** A turn that passed without a move. */\n    public record Notice(NoticeKind kind, Side side) {\n    }\n}\n"

  "content": "package com.threeclassics.backgammon;\n\nimport com.threeclassics.backgammon.BackgammonMove.Step;\nimport java.util.ArrayList;\nimport java.util.LinkedHashMap;\nimport java.util.List;\nimport java.util.Map;\n\n/**\n * Generates every legal way to play a roll.\n *\n * <p>A depth-first search tries the dice in both orders (or four times for doubles) and records each\n * sequence where no die can be played further. Then the rules filter it: the player must use as many\n * dice as possible, and if only one die can be used and either could be, it must be the larger one.\n */\nfinal class Turns {\n\n    private Turns() {\n    }\n\n    /** Every legal step sequence, in order of play. Empty if the roll can't be used at all. */\n    static List<List<Step>> legal(Position position, int die1, int die2) {\n        List<List<Step>> all = new ArrayList<>();\n        int[] dice = die1 == die2 ? new int[] {die1, die1, die1, die1} : new int[] {die1, die2};\n        search(position, dice, new boolean[dice.length], new ArrayList<>(), all);\n\n        int most = all.stream().mapToInt(List::size).max().orElse(0);\n        if (most == 0) {\n            return List.of();\n        }\n        List<List<Step>> longest = all.stream().filter(sequence -> sequence.size() == most).toList();\n        if (most == 1 && die1 != die2) {\n            int larger = Math.max(die1, die2);\n            boolean largerPlayable = longest.stream().anyMatch(sequence -> sequence.getFirst().die() == larger);\n            if (largerPlayable) {\n                return longest.stream().filter(sequence -> sequence.getFirst().die() == larger).toList();\n            }\n        }\n        return longest;\n    }\n\n    /** The legal sequences with one representative per distinct resulting position. */\n    static List<List<Step>> distinct(Position position, List<List<Step>> sequences) {\n        Map<String, List<Step>> byResult = new LinkedHashMap<>();\n        for (List<Step> sequence : sequences) {\n            byResult.putIfAbsent(result(position, sequence).key(), sequence);\n        }\n        return new ArrayList<>(byResult.values());\n    }\n\n    static Position result(Position position, List<Step> sequence) {\n        Position next = position.copy();\n        sequence.forEach(next::apply);\n        return next;\n    }\n\n    private static void search(Position position, int[] dice, boolean[] used, List<Step> sequence, List<List<Step>> out) {\n        boolean moved = false;\n        // For doubles every die is the same, so only the first unused one needs trying.\n        boolean doubles = dice.length == 4;\n        for (int i = 0; i < dice.length; i++) {\n            if (used[i]) continue;\n            if (i > 0 && !doubles && dice[i] == dice[i - 1] && !used[i - 1]) continue;\n            List<Step> steps = position.steps(dice[i]);\n            for (Step step : steps) {\n                moved = true;\n                Position next = position.copy();\n                next.apply(step);\n                used[i] = true;\n                sequence.add(step);\n                search(next, dice, used, sequence, out);\n                sequence.removeLast();\n                used[i] = false;\n            }\n            if (doubles) break;\n        }\n        if (!moved) {\n            out.add(List.copyOf(sequence));\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "package com.threeclassics.backgammon;\n\nimport com.threeclassics.backgammon.BackgammonState.Phase;\nimport com.threeclassics.core.Side;\nimport java.util.ArrayList;\nimport java.util.Arrays;\nimport java.util.List;\n\n/**\n * Builds backgammon positions with each side counted in its own numbering. Checkers not placed on\n * the board or bar are borne off, so each side always totals 15.\n */\nfinal class Board {\n\n    private final int[] ivory = new int[26];\n    private final int[] obsidian = new int[26];\n\n    static Board empty() {\n        return new Board();\n    }\n\n    /** P1 checkers on P1's point. */\n    Board ivory(int point, int count) {\n        ivory[point] += count;\n        return this;\n    }\n\n    /** P2 checkers on P2's own point. */\n    Board obsidian(int point, int count) {\n        obsidian[point] += count;\n        return this;\n    }\n\n    Board ivoryBar(int count) {\n        return ivory(25, count);\n    }\n\n    Board obsidianBar(int count) {\n        return obsidian(25, count);\n    }\n\n    BackgammonState toMove(Side side, int die1, int die2) {\n        return state(side, Phase.MOVE, List.of(die1, die2));\n    }\n\n    BackgammonState toRoll(Side side) {\n        return state(side, Phase.ROLL, List.of());\n    }\n\n    private BackgammonState state(Side side, Phase phase, List<Integer> dice) {\n        List<Integer> points = new ArrayList<>();\n        for (int p = 1; p <= 24; p++) {\n            points.add(ivory[p] - obsidian[25 - p]);\n        }\n        int ivoryLeft = Arrays.stream(ivory).sum();\n        int obsidianLeft = Arrays.stream(obsidian).sum();\n        return new BackgammonState(points, ivory[25], obsidian[25], 15 - ivoryLeft, 15 - obsidianLeft,\n                side, phase, dice, null, List.of(), null);\n    }\n}\n"
}

a <= 6; a++) {\n            for (int b = 1; b <= 6; b++) {\n                BackgammonState state = engine.roll(engine.apply(engine.initialState(), BackgammonMove.ROLL, new ScriptedDice(2, 1)), a, b);\n                state = Board.empty()\n                        .ivory(24, 2).ivory(13, 5).ivory(8, 3).ivory(6, 5)\n                        .obsidian(24, 2).obsidian(13, 5).obsidian(8, 3).obsidian(6, 5)\n                        .toMove(Side.P1, a, b);\n                long start = System.nanoTime();\n                BackgammonMove chosen = ai.chooseMove(state, Difficulty.HARD, new Random(1), Duration.ofSeconds(1));\n                long elapsedMs = (System.nanoTime() - start) / 1_000_000;\n                assertThat(elapsedMs).as(\"roll %d-%d\", a, b).isLessThan(2000);\n                assertThat(engine.legalMoves(state)).contains(chosen);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void hardHitsAnExposedBlotInItsHomeBoard() {\n        // Obsidian has a lone checker on Ivory's 5-point; 8/5* hits it and makes Ivory safer.\n        BackgammonState state = Board.empty()\n                .ivory(8, 3).ivory(6, 5).ivory(13, 5).ivory(24, 2)\n                .obsidian(20, 1).obsidian(13, 5).obsidian(8, 3).obsidian(6, 5).obsidian(24, 1)\n                .toMove(Side.P1, 3, 1);\n        BackgammonMove chosen = ai.chooseMove(state, Difficulty.HARD, new Random(1), Duration.ofSeconds(1));\n        assertThat(chosen.steps()).anyMatch(BackgammonMove.Step::hit);\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void mediumMakesThePointOnAThreeOne() {\n        // The classic 3-1 opening: 8/5 6/5 makes the 5-point.\n        BackgammonState state = Board.empty()\n                .ivory(24, 2).ivory(13, 5).ivory(8, 3).ivory(6, 5)\n                .obsidian(24, 2).obsidian(13, 5).obsidian(8, 3).obsidian(6, 5)\n                .toMove(Side.P1, 3, 1);\n        BackgammonState after = engine.apply(state,\n                ai.chooseMove(state, Difficulty.MEDIUM, new Random(1), Duration.ofSeconds(1)), new ScriptedDice());\n        assertThat(after.points().get(4)).isEqualTo(2);\n    }\n}\n"

Claude’s reasoning
The worst roll gives 9,085 orderings (1.8 MB of JSON) because doubles let the same steps be clicked in any order, so I'm merging them into a step graph where every root-to-complete path is a legal turn. Measuring that graph's size comes next.

{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\backend\\src\\main\\java\\com\\threeclassics\\backgammon\\TurnGraph.java",
  "content": "package com.threeclassics.backgammon;\n\nimport com.threeclassics.backgammon.BackgammonMove.Step;\nimport java.util.ArrayList;\nimport java.util.Arrays;\nimport java.util.HashMap;\nimport java.util.List;\nimport java.util.Map;\n\n/**\n * Every legal way to play a roll, as a graph the client can walk one step at a time.\n *\n * <p>Node 0 is the start of the turn. Each node is a distinct intermediate position (with the dice\n * still unused), so the many orders in which doubles can be played share nodes instead of being\n * listed one by one. Every path from node 0 to a {@code complete} node is a legal turn.\n *\n * @param nodes each node's outgoing steps as {@code [from, to, die, hit (0/1), child]}\n */\npublic record TurnGraph(List<Node> nodes) {\n\n    public record Node(List<int[]> steps, boolean complete) {\n    }\n\n    static TurnGraph of(Position start, List<List<Step>> sequences) {\n        List<List<int[]>> edges = new ArrayList<>();\n        List<Boolean> complete = new ArrayList<>();\n        Map<String, Integer> ids = new HashMap<>();\n        edges.add(new ArrayList<>());\n        complete.add(false);\n\n        for (List<Step> sequence : sequences) {\n            Position position = start.copy();\n            int node = 0;\n            List<Integer> used = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < sequence.size(); i++) {\n                Step step = sequence.get(i);\n                position.apply(step);\n                used.add(step.die());\n                int[] sortedUsed = used.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sorted().toArray();\n                String key = position.key() + Arrays.toString(sortedUsed);\n                Integer child = ids.get(key);\n                if (child == null) {\n                    child = edges.size();\n                    ids.put(key, child);\n                    edges.add(new ArrayList<>());\n                    complete.add(i == sequence.size() - 1);\n                }\n                int target = child;\n                boolean known = edges.get(node).stream().anyMatch(e -> e[0] == step.from() && e[1] == step.to() && e[2] == step.die());\n                if (!known) {\n                    edges.get(node).add(new int[] {step.from(), step.to(), step.die(), step.hit() ? 1 : 0, target});\n                }\n                node = target;\n            }\n        }\n\n        List<Node> nodes = new ArrayList<>();\n        for (int i = 0; i < edges.size(); i++) {\n            nodes.add(new Node(edges.get(i), complete.get(i)));\n        }\n        return new TurnGraph(nodes);\n    }\n}\n"
}

            // Each distinct result is offered once to the client.
            assertThat(engine.clientMoves(state).size()).isLessThanOrEqualTo(paths.size());
        }
    }

    private static void walk(TurnGraph graph, int node, List<Step> path, Set<List<Step>> out) {
        if (graph.nodes().get(node).complete()) {
            out.add(List.copyOf(path));
        }
        for (int[] edge : graph.nodes().get(node).steps()) {
            path.add(new Step(edge[0], edge[1], edge[2], edge[3] == 1));
            walk(graph, edge[4], path, out);
            path.removeLast();
        }
    }

    void notationNamesTheBarHitsAndBearingOff() {""")

Turn generation searches both dice orders (four steps for doubles), then
applies the max-dice and larger-die rules. Covers bar entry, closeouts,
blocked points, hits, bearing off from the highest point and single,
gammon and backgammon scoring. Legal turns reach the client as a step
graph that merges equivalent orders, so doubles stay small on the wire.

  "content": "// Board geometry in SVG user units, drawn from P1's (the human's) side: home board bottom-right,\n// checkers travelling counter-clockwise from the top-right, bar down the middle, tray on the right.\nimport type { Side } from '../../api/types';\nimport { BAR, OFF, type BackgammonState, type Step } from './types';\n\nexport const FRAME = 24;\nexport const POINT_W = 66;\nexport const BAR_W = 64;\nexport const TRAY_W = 100;\nexport const R = 30;\nexport const POINT_H = 5 * 2 * R;\nexport const MID_GAP = 80;\nexport const HALF_W = 6 * POINT_W;\nexport const VIEW_W = FRAME + HALF_W + BAR_W + HALF_W + TRAY_W + FRAME;\nexport const VIEW_H = FRAME + POINT_H + MID_GAP + POINT_H + FRAME;\nexport const BAR_X = FRAME + HALF_W + BAR_W / 2;\nexport const TRAY_X = VIEW_W - FRAME - TRAY_W;\n/** Stacks show at most five checkers; a badge on the fifth gives the count. */\nexport const MAX_STACK = 5;\nexport const OFF_SCALE = 0.42;\n\n/**\n * Screen slot of P1's point p (1–24). The bottom row holds 12…1 from left to right, the top row\n * 13…24, so P1's 1-point is bottom-right and its 24-point top-right.\n */\nexport function pointSlot(point: number): { column: number; top: boolean } {\n  return point <= 12 ? { column: 12 - point, top: false } : { column: point - 13, top: true };\n}\n\nexport function columnX(column: number): number {\n  return FRAME + column * POINT_W + (column >= 6 ? BAR_W : 0);\n}\n\n/** Centre of the n-th checker (0 = base) on P1's point p. */\nexport function checkerOnPoint(point: number, index: number): { x: number; y: number } {\n  const { column, top } = pointSlot(point);\n  const i = Math.min(index, MAX_STACK - 1);\n  const x = columnX(column) + POINT_W / 2;\n  return { x, y: top ? FRAME + R + i * 2 * R : VIEW_H - FRAME - R - i * 2 * R };\n}\n\n/** P1's bar checkers sit below the middle, P2's above it. */\nexport function checkerOnBar(side: Side, index: number): { x: number; y: number } {\n  const offset = MID_GAP / 2 - R + 6 + (Math.min(index, 3) + 1) * 2 * R - R;\n  return { x: BAR_X, y: side === 'P1' ? VIEW_H / 2 + offset : VIEW_H / 2 - offset };\n}\n\n/** Borne-off checkers fill a 3 × 5 grid in the tray: P1's at the bottom, P2's at the top. */\nexport function checkerOff(side: Side, index: number): { x: number; y: number } {\n  const column = index % 3;\n  const row = Math.floor(index / 3);\n  const x = TRAY_X + 22 + column * 28;\n  const y = side === 'P1' ? VIEW_H - FRAME - 18 - row * 28 : FRAME + 18 + row * 28;\n  return { x, y };\n}\n\n/** A mover's own point number as P1's point number (the screen's numbering). */\nexport function toScreenPoint(point: number, side: Side): number {\n  return side === 'P1' ? point : 25 - point;\n}\n\nexport function pipCount(state: BackgammonState, side: Side): number {\n  let pips = 25 * (side === 'P1' ? state.barP1 : state.barP2);\n  state.points.forEach((count, i) => {\n    if (side === 'P1' && count > 0) pips += (i + 1) * count;\n    if (side === 'P2' && count < 0) pips += (24 - i) * -count;\n  });\n  return pips;\n}\n\n/** The board right after one step, drawn while the human builds a turn or a turn animates. */\nexport function applyStep(state: BackgammonState, side: Side, step: Step): BackgammonState {\n  const points = [...state.points];\n  const sign = side === 'P1' ? 1 : -1;\n  let { barP1, barP2, offP1, offP2 } = state;\n  if (step.from === BAR) {\n    if (side === 'P1') barP1--;\n    else barP2--;\n  } else {\n    points[toScreenPoint(step.from, side) - 1] -= sign;\n  }\n  if (step.to === OFF) {\n    if (side === 'P1') offP1++;\n    else offP2++;\n  } else {\n    const index = toScreenPoint(step.to, side) - 1;\n    if (points[index] === -sign) {\n      points[index] = 0;\n      if (side === 'P1') barP2++;\n      else barP1++;\n    }\n    points[index] += sign;\n  }\n  return { ...state, points, barP1, barP2, offP1, offP2 };\n}\n"
}

p > 13; p--) expect(checkerOnPoint(p - 1, 0).x).toBeLessThan(checkerOnPoint(p, 0).x);\n    expect(checkerOnPoint(12, 0).x).toBe(checkerOnPoint(13, 0).x);\n    for (let p = 12; p > 1; p--) expect(checkerOnPoint(p - 1, 0).x).toBeGreaterThan(checkerOnPoint(p, 0).x);\n  });\n\n  it('keeps every stack, even a tall one, inside its half of the board', () => {\n    for (let p = 1;   "content": "// Walking the server's turn graph: the player builds a turn one checker step at a time, and only\n// steps that continue some legal turn are ever offered.\nimport type { Step, TurnGraph } from './types';\n\nexport interface GraphStep extends Step {\n  child: number;\n}\n\n/** The legal next steps after the given path of graph nodes (path[0] is always node 0). */\nexport function stepsFrom(graph: TurnGraph, path: number[]): GraphStep[] {\n  const node = graph.nodes[path[path.length - 1]];\n  return node.steps.map(([from, to, die, hit, child]) => ({ from, to, die, hit: hit === 1, child }));\n}\n\nexport function isComplete(graph: TurnGraph, path: number[]): boolean {\n  return graph.nodes[path[path.length - 1]].complete;\n}\n\n/** Locations (mover's numbering, 25 = bar) that have a checker able to move next. */\nexport function movableFrom(graph: TurnGraph, path: number[]): number[] {\n  return [...new Set(stepsFrom(graph, path).map((step) => step.from))];\n}\n\n/**\n * The step for moving a checker from one location to another. When several dice reach the same\n * place (bearing off with a 5 or a 6), the smallest is used and the larger saved.\n */\nexport function stepBetween(graph: TurnGraph, path: number[], from: number, to: number): GraphStep | null {\n  const options = stepsFrom(graph, path).filter((step) => step.from === from && step.to === to);\n  options.sort((a, b) => a.die - b.die);\n  return options[0] ?? null;\n}\n\n/** The dice still to be played after the given steps, for dimming used dice. */\nexport function remainingDice(dice: number[], steps: Step[]): boolean[] {\n  const all = dice[0] === dice[1] ? [dice[0], dice[0], dice[0], dice[0]] : [...dice];\n  const used = all.map(() => false);\n  for (const step of steps) {\n    const index = all.findIndex((die, i) => !used[i] && die === step.die);\n    if (index >= 0) used[index] = true;\n  }\n  return used.map((u) => !u);\n}\n"
}

  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\frontend\\src\\games\\backgammon\\stacks.ts",
  "content": "// Gives every checker a stable identity so that moves can slide it from place to place. Identities\n// are assigned in a fixed order from a base position, then replayed through the steps since then.\nimport type { Side } from '../../api/types';\nimport { toScreenPoint } from './geometry';\nimport { BAR, OFF, type BackgammonState, type Step } from './types';\n\n/** Stack keys: \"p1\"…\"p24\" (P1's numbering), \"barP1\", \"barP2\", \"offP1\", \"offP2\". */\nexport type Stacks = Record<string, string[]>;\n\nexport interface Placed {\n  id: string;\n  side: Side;\n  key: string;\n  index: number;\n  /** How many checkers share the stack (for the count badge). */\n  size: number;\n}\n\nexport function initialStacks(state: BackgammonState): Stacks {\n  const stacks: Stacks = {};\n  let ivory = 0;\n  let obsidian = 0;\n  const fill = (key: string, side: Side, count: number) => {\n    stacks[key] = Array.from({ length: count }, () => (side === 'P1' ? `i${ivory++}` : `o${obsidian++}`));\n  };\n  fill('barP1', 'P1', state.barP1);\n  fill('barP2', 'P2', state.barP2);\n  state.points.forEach((count, i) => fill(`p${i + 1}`, count > 0 ? 'P1' : 'P2', Math.abs(count)));\n  fill('offP1', 'P1', state.offP1);\n  fill('offP2', 'P2', state.offP2);\n  return stacks;\n}\n\nexport function locationKey(location: number, side: Side): string {\n  if (location === BAR) return `bar${side}`;\n  if (location === OFF) return `off${side}`;\n  return `p${toScreenPoint(location, side)}`;\n}\n\n/** Plays one step on the stacks: the mover's top checker moves; a hit blot goes to the bar. */\nexport function replay(stacks: Stacks, side: Side, step: Step): Stacks {\n  const next: Stacks = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(stacks).map(([key, ids]) => [key, [...ids]]));\n  const from = locationKey(step.from, side);\n  const to = locationKey(step.to, side);\n  const moving = next[from].pop();\n  if (!moving) return stacks;\n  const ownPrefix = side === 'P1' ? 'i' : 'o';\n  if (to.startsWith('p') && next[to].length === 1 && !next[to][0].startsWith(ownPrefix)) {\n    const opponent: Side = side === 'P1' ? 'P2' : 'P1';\n    next[`bar${opponent}`].push(next[to].pop()!);\n  }\n  next[to].push(moving);\n  return next;\n}\n\nexport function placed(stacks: Stacks): Placed[] {\n  const all: Placed[] = [];\n  for (const [key, ids] of Object.entries(stacks)) {\n    ids.forEach((id, index) => all.push({ id, side: id.startsWith('i') ? 'P1' : 'P2', key, index, size: ids.length }));\n  }\n  return all;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "export function BackgammonRules() {\n  return (\n    <>\n      <h3>Goal</h3>\n      <p>Bring all 15 of your checkers into your home board (bottom right), then bear them all off before your opponent does.</p>\n\n      <h3>Starting</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>Each side rolls one die. The higher roll starts and plays both of those dice. Ties roll again.</li>\n        <li>After that, players take turns rolling two dice.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3>Moving</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>Your checkers travel counter-clockwise: across the top from the right, down the left, then along the bottom into home.</li>\n        <li>Each die is a separate move. One checker can use both dice if it can land after the first one.</li>\n        <li>Doubles are played four times.</li>\n        <li>You may land on an empty point, your own point, or a point with a single opposing checker, which sends it to the bar. Two or more opposing checkers block a point, but you can jump over it.</li>\n        <li>Use as many dice as you legally can. If only one die can be played, play the larger one if it fits. With no legal move, the turn passes.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3>The bar</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>Checkers on the bar must come back in first, into your opponent's home board: a 3 enters on their 3-point.</li>\n        <li>If all six of those points are blocked you're closed out, and your turn passes until one opens.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3>Bearing off</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>Once all 15 checkers are home, a die removes a checker from the matching point.</li>\n        <li>With no checker there, you must move one from a higher point. If there are none higher, bear off from your highest point.</li>\n        <li>If one of your checkers is hit, it must come back around before you can bear off again.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3>Scoring</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>A single game is 1 point. If your opponent hasn't borne off any checkers, it's a gammon (2). If they also still have a checker on the bar or in your home board, it's a backgammon (3).</li>\n        <li>There's no doubling cube in this version.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3>Controls</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li>Roll, click a checker (or the bar) to see where it can go, then click a glowing point or the tray.</li>\n        <li>Undo takes back a step. Confirm ends your turn once all your dice are played.</li>\n      </ul>\n    </>\n  );\n}\n"
}

Bash Log backgammon decisions and commit Milestone 4
cd /c/Users/ustec/Downloads/Chess_Project && cat >> docs/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

## Backgammon

- **Points from P1's side, steps in the mover's own numbering.** The state stores 24 signed counts
  from Ivory's point of view; every step uses the mover's numbers (25 = bar, 0 = off), matching how
  players write moves. A bar entry with a die of n lands on the mover's point 25 − n, the opponent's
  n-point.
- **Turn generation follows the brief's recipe:** DFS over both dice orders (four steps for doubles),
  keep the longest sequences (max-dice rule), and if only one die fits, keep the larger.
- **The client gets a step graph, not every ordering.** Doubles can be played in thousands of orders:
  measured over 300 games, the worst roll had 9,085 ordered sequences (1.8 MB of JSON). The server
  now merges orderings that reach the same intermediate position into a graph (worst case 62 KB,
  average under 2 KB). The client walks it one checker step at a time, so any legal order is
  accepted and nothing illegal is offered. `legalMoves` lists one turn per distinct result, and the
  server still validates the submitted turn against every legal ordering.
- **Passing is automatic and announced.** A roll with no legal play, or being closed out, passes the
  turn inside the engine and is recorded as a notice in the state, which the client turns into a
  short toast. A closed-out player doesn't roll at all.
- **Standard scoring, not the PDF's.** Single 1, gammon 2, backgammon 3. The rulebook's "count the
  loser's remaining checkers" variant is not used.
- **No doubling cube in v1.** A deliberate cut: single games only, so no Crawford or money-play rules.
- **Hard** prunes to the eight best candidates by the static evaluation, then scores each by the
  opponent's best reply averaged over all 21 rolls. In a pure race it plays greedily on pip count,
  which is close to optimal there.
- **Checkers have identities on the client.** Each checker gets an id from a base position, replayed
  through the steps since then, so moves, hits (to the bar) and bear-offs (to the tray) all slide.
  Stacks over five show a count badge instead of overflowing the point.
EOF
git add -A 2>/dev/null && git commit -q -m "Add backgammon client with desert scene

Roll, then build the turn checker by checker through the server's step
graph, with Undo and Confirm. Dice tumble, used dice dim, checkers slide
to points, the bar and the tray, and passed turns are announced. Adds
the desert scene, Vitest for the graph walker and board orientation, and
Playwright coverage for all three games.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline | head -2

import re
p='app/settings.tsx'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old="""  const [ambientMotion, setAmbientMotion] = useState<boolean>(() => {
    const stored = readJson<{ ambientMotion?: boolean }>(STORAGE_KEY, {});
    return stored.ambientMotion ?? !prefersReducedMotion();
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    writeJson(STORAGE_KEY, { ambientMotion });
  }, [ambientMotion]);

  const value = useMemo(() => ({ ambientMotion, setAmbientMotion }), [ambientMotion]);"""
new="""  // Until the player chooses, follow the system's reduced-motion preference (and its changes).
  const [choice, setChoice] = useState<boolean | undefined>(() => readJson<{ ambientMotion?: boolean }>(STORAGE_KEY, {}).ambientMotion);
  const [reduced, setReduced] = useState(prefersReducedMotion);

  useEffect(() => {
    const query = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
    const onChange = () => setReduced(query.matches);
    query.addEventListener('change', onChange);
    return () => query.removeEventListener('change', onChange);
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo(
    () => ({
      ambientMotion: choice ?? !reduced,
      setAmbientMotion: (on: boolean) => {
        setChoice(on);
        writeJson(STORAGE_KEY, { ambientMotion: on });
      },
    }),
    [choice, reduced],
  );"""

Bash Compute WCAG contrast ratios for theme colors
node -e '
const hex=h=>{h=h.replace("#","");return [0,2,4].map(i=>parseInt(h.slice(i,i+2),16)/255)};
const lum=c=>{const [r,g,b]=c.map(v=>v<=0.03928?v/12.92:Math.pow((v+0.055)/1.055,2.4));return 0.2126*r+0.7152*g+0.0722*b};
const ratio=(a,b)=>{const [x,y]=[lum(hex(a)),lum(hex(b))].sort((p,q)=>q-p);return ((x+0.05)/(y+0.05)).toFixed(2)};
const pairs=[
["ocean text/surface","#e9f6f8","#072b3b"],["ocean muted/surface","#9cc6ce","#072b3b"],["ocean primary btn","#04202f","#5cc8d0"],["ocean selected seg","#072b3b","#e9f6f8"],
["winter text/surface","#eef3f8","#18243b"],["winter muted/surface","#a9bdd6","#18243b"],["winter primary btn","#2a1a08","#f2c48d"],
["desert text/surface","#f6efe2","#34200f"],["desert muted/surface","#d9c3a5","#34200f"],["desert primary btn","#2b1a12","#e8cfa4"],["desert tray count","#e8cfa4","#3b1f12"],
["jungle text/card","#0f2619","#f4f1e8"],["jungle muted/card","#4a5d50","#f4f1e8"],["jungle play btn","#ffffff","#2f8f86"],["jungle wordmark","#f4f1e8","#16301f"],
["toast","#18243b","#eef3f8"]];
for (const [n,a,b] of pairs) console.log(n.padEnd(22), ratio(a,b));
'

  "content": "import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';\nimport { connectFour, moveItems, startFromPosition, waitForHumanTurn } from './games';\n\ntest.describe('keyboard', () => {\n  test('Connect Four: arrows choose a column and Enter drops a disc', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/connect-four');\n    await waitForHumanTurn(page);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Column 4,/ }).focus();\n    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Column 5,/ })).toBeFocused();\n    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n    await expect.poll(() => moveItems(page).count()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);\n    await expect(moveItems(page).first()).toContainText('Column 5');\n  });\n\n  test('Checkers: arrows move between squares and Enter selects and moves', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/checkers');\n    await waitForHumanTurn(page);\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^c3,/ }).focus();\n    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /^c3, .*selected/ })).toBeVisible();\n    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');\n    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /^d4,/ })).toBeFocused();\n    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n    await expect.poll(() => moveItems(page).count()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);\n    await expect(moveItems(page).first()).toContainText('c3–d4');\n  });\n\n  test('the result modal traps focus, Esc closes it, and the pill reopens it', async ({ page, request }) => {\n    await startFromPosition(page, request, connectFour);\n    await waitForHumanTurn(page);\n    await connectFour.win(page);\n    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');\n    await expect(dialog.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play again' })).toBeFocused();\n    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');\n      expect(await dialog.evaluate((node) => node.contains(document.activeElement))).toBe(true);\n    }\n    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');\n    await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Show result' }).click();\n    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  test('home cards are reached with Tab and opened with Enter', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/');\n    const card = page.getByRole('link', { name: /Checkers$/ });\n    for (let i = 0; i < 6 && !(await card.evaluate((node) => node === document.activeElement)); i++) {\n      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');\n    }\n    await expect(card).toBeFocused();\n    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\\/checkers$/);\n  });\n});\n\ntest.describe('reduced motion', () => {\n  test.use({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });\n\n  test('scenes stay still when the system asks for less motion', async ({ page }) => {\n    for (const path of ['/', '/connect-four', '/checkers', '/backgammon']) {\n      await page.goto(path);\n      const scenes = page.locator('[data-scene]');\n      await expect(scenes.first()).toBeAttached();\n      for (const animate of await scenes.evaluateAll((nodes) => nodes.map((node) => node.getAttribute('data-animate')))) {\n        expect(animate).toBe('false');\n      }\n    }\n  });\n\n  test('the setting can turn ambient motion back on', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/connect-four');\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Settings' }).click();\n    await page.getByRole('switch', { name: /Ambient motion/ }).click();\n    await expect(page.locator('[data-scene]').first()).toHaveAttribute('data-animate', 'true');\n  });\n});\n"
}

JAR=$(ls ~/.m2/repository/org/yaml/snakeyaml/*/snakeyaml-*.jar | grep -v sources | tail -1) && echo "$JAR" && cat > /c/Users/ustec/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-ustec-Downloads-Chess-Project/217c3c62-651f-4afc-a9df-59c61ee27484/scratchpad/CheckYaml.java <<'EOF'
import java.nio.file.*;
import org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml;

public class CheckYaml {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        for (String file : args) {
            int docs = 0;
            for (Object doc : new Yaml().loadAll(Files.readString(Path.of(file)))) {
                if (doc != null) docs++;
                if (doc instanceof java.util.Map<?, ?> m && m.containsKey("kind")) {
                    System.out.println("  " + file + ": " + m.get("kind") + " " + ((java.util.Map<?, ?>) m.get("metadata")).get("name"));

  "content": "# Three Classics\n\nConnect Four, Checkers and Backgammon, each played against the computer at three levels or by two\npeople on one device. Every rule and every computer move is decided by a Java server that acts as the\nreferee; the React client draws the board, offers only the moves the server says are legal, and\nanimates what happened. Each game lives in its own quiet, animated world — an ocean, a winter\nevening, a desert at dusk — with a jungle home page to step out from.\n\n| Home | Connect Four | Checkers | Backgammon |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| ![Home](docs/screenshots/home-1440x900.png) | ![Connect Four](docs/screenshots/connect-four-1440x900.png) | ![Checkers](docs/screenshots/checkers-1440x900.png) | ![Backgammon](docs/screenshots/backgammon-1440x900.png) |\n\n## Quick start\n\nNeeds Docker with Compose.\n\n```bash\ndocker compose up --build\n```\n\nThen open http://localhost:8080. Nothing to configure: every setting has a working default, and\n`.env.example` lists the ones you can override (copy it to `.env`).\n\n`make up` / `make down` do the same in the background.\n\n## What you can do\n\n- Play against the computer on Easy, Medium or Hard, or switch to two players on one device.\n- Choose to go first or second (Connect Four) or to play Dark or Light (Checkers; the board turns so\n  your pieces are at the bottom). In Backgammon the opening roll decides.\n- Click a piece to see where it can go; illegal clicks just shake. Multi-jumps and backgammon turns are\n  built one step at a time, with Undo and Confirm for backgammon.\n- Refresh at any time: the game resumes. The home page shows your record per game and offers Continue.\n- Rules drawer, last-move highlights, result modal with Play again at any level, keyboard play\n  throughout, and an ambient-motion switch that defaults to off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n\n## Running the tests\n\n| What | Command | Notes |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Backend unit + integration | `cd backend && ./mvnw test` | Rules, AI, a 500-game soak per game, and API tests. API tests use Testcontainers when Docker is running, or any Postgres via `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (+ `TEST_DATABASE_USER`/`PASSWORD`). |\n| Frontend unit (Vitest) | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Legal-prefix matcher, backgammon turn-graph walker, board coordinate mapping for all three boards. |\n| End-to-end + layout (Playwright) | `make e2e` | Starts the compose stack with the dev profile, then runs every spec against http://localhost:8080. |\n| Screenshots | `cd frontend && SCREENSHOTS=1 npx playwright test screenshots` | Rewrites `docs/screenshots/`. |\n\n`make test` runs the backend and Vitest suites.\n\nThe Playwright suite covers, for every game: home → game → move → computer replies → restart → home;\na near-win position → result modal → Play again; resume after refresh; keyboard play; the focus trap;\nreduced motion; and layout checks at 1280×720, 1440×900, 1920×1080 and 390×844 (board fully visible\nand centred within 2 px, no scrollbars, identical cell sizes, cells unchanged across a move and the\nreply, nothing covering the board).\n\nTo run the e2e tests without Docker, start the backend with the dev profile and the Vite dev server,\nthen run Playwright (it defaults to http://localhost:5173):\n\n```bash\ncd backend && ./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=dev\n```\n\n```bash\ncd frontend && npm run dev\n```\n\n```bash\ncd frontend && npx playwright test\n```\n\n## Kubernetes\n\nThe same stack runs on a local [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) cluster with the Kustomize\nmanifests in `k8s/` (namespace, Postgres StatefulSet with a PVC and Secret, backend and frontend\nDeployments and Services with probes, and a ConfigMap).\n\n```bash\nmake k8s-up\n```\n\nThat creates the cluster, builds both images, loads them into kind, applies `k8s/`, waits for the\nrollouts and port-forwards http://localhost:8080.   "new_string": "# Decisions\n\n## The main decisions\n\n1. **The server is the referee.** All rules and all computer play are in the Java backend. The client\n   draws the state, offers only the server's `legalMoves`, and sends back the one the player picked;\n   the server validates, applies, lets the computer reply and persists, in one transaction. One source\n   of truth, rules that are unit-tested in isolation, and no way to cheat from the browser.\n2. **Multi-step moves are legal paths matched by prefix.** A checkers multi-jump arrives as a complete\n   path; the client accepts a click only if the squares so far are a prefix of some legal path, and\n   submits when a path is complete. Backgammon turns use the same idea through a step graph, because\n   listing every ordering of a double was measured at up to 1.8 MB (see Backgammon below).\n3. **Boards are single SVGs with a fixed viewBox.** Cells and pieces are drawn in fixed coordinates and\n   the SVG scales as a whole, so nothing can change size with content. Highlights are fills, rings and\n   transforms only, and a Playwright layout test checks every cell's size and position across moves.\n4. **Scenes are procedural, not photos.** Each theme is layered SVG silhouettes plus CSS gradients and\n   one particle canvas, all driven by a single shared `requestAnimationFrame` loop that pauses when\n   the tab is hidden. That keeps the repo free of licensing questions, scales to any screen and can\n   go fully still for reduced motion. A licensed photo could be dropped in via `--scene-photo`.\n5. **Three games, one engine interface.** `GameEngine<S, M>` and `AiPlayer<S, M>` are implemented per\n   game and registered as a `GameModule`. The service, API, persistence, session hook and page shell\n   are written once; each game adds an engine, an AI, a board and its rules text.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n- **No doubling cube.** Backgammon is played as single games, scored 1/2/3 for single, gammon and\n  backgammon. The cube (and the Crawford, Jacoby and beaver rules that come with matches and money\n  play) was the first thing to cut for time.\n- **Standard scoring rather than the reference PDF's.** The PDF scores a game by counting the loser's\n  remaining checkers; the brief and standard play use single/gammon/backgammon, so that's what is used.\n- **No accounts.** One local player; stats are computed from finished games in the database.\n- **Spring Boot 3.5, not 4.x**, to keep to APIs I know well inside the time budget.\n- **No Docker on the build machine.** Everything except the containers was run and tested (backend\n  against a local PostgreSQL 16, Playwright against the dev server and the production bundle). The\n  Dockerfiles, compose file and Kubernetes manifests are written and their YAML is validated, but\n  `docker compose up` and kind were not run here. That is the first thing to verify.\n- **AI depth is budgeted, not fixed.** Hard searches as deep as it can in about 0.85 s, so its strength\n  depends a little on the machine. Medium and Easy are deterministic in effort.\n- **The client draws its own move before the server confirms it.** This keeps input instant. All seven milestones from the brief are built and committed (9 commits in a new repo in `Chess_Project`): Connect Four, Checkers and Backgammon, each at Easy/Medium/Hard or two players, plus the jungle home page. I couldn't run `docker compose up --build` or the kind deployment, because this machine has no Docker. Those files are written and their YAML parses, so the first thing to check is running `make up` and `make k8s-up` on a machine with Docker. **Test results** (all passing locally): - **Backend:** 94 tests against a local PostgreSQL 16. They cover every rule case the brief lists for the three games, the AI win/block and 2-second checks, 500 Easy-vs-Easy games per game, and the API's 400/409/dev-endpoint checks. - **Vitest:** 26 tests, covering the click-by-click move matcher and the board coordinate mapping for all three boards. - **Playwright:** 27 tests, run against both the dev server and the production build. They cover each game end to end, a near-win → result modal → Play again, resume after refresh, keyboard play, the modal focus trap, reduced motion, and layout at 1280×720, 1440×900, 1920×1080 and 390×844. - **Screenshots:** I reviewed them at all four sizes and fixed what they showed (a stray shadow, contrast, Home and Backgammon layout); the final set is in `docs/screenshots/`. **Where I departed from the brief (all logged in [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md)):** - **Backgammon move list:** listing every ordering of a double reached 9,085 sequences (1.8 MB) on one roll. The server now sends a graph of steps that merges equivalent orders (62 KB at worst), and the client still accepts only legal next steps. - **Create game:** it returns the same response as a move instead of a bare game, so the computer's opening move animates like any other reply. - **Spring Boot 3.5 instead of 4.x:** to stay on APIs I know well within the time budget. - **JDK 25 for local builds, targeting Java 21:** the system JDK is 17; the containers use Temurin 21. - **Vite 6:** newer versions need a newer Node than your 20.17. - **Not added:** `@types/node` and jsdom aren't on the approved list, and I didn't need them. - **Moodboards:** kept out of git, since they're other people's photos. - **Left out:** the stretch goals (hint, takeback, sound, doubling cube). **What's left for you:** - Export this session's transcript into `docs/agent-transcripts/`. - Correct [docs/TIME_LOG.md](docs/TIME_LOG.md); it's built from commit times, about 2 hours of agent time. - To try it now, the dev stack is still running at http://localhost:5173. The backend and the portable Postgres are in my temp folder, outside the project. [README.md](README.md) covers setup, tests, the kind flow, the architecture diagrams and how each AI plays.

Claude’s reasoning
The backend crashed on cold start because Postgres wasn't ready, so Flyway failed and Kubernetes kept restarting it. I'm adding an init container that waits on pg_isready so startup stops depending on crash loops.
Edit C:\Users\ustec\Downloads\Chess_Project\k8s\backend.yaml
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\k8s\\backend.yaml",
  "old_string": "    spec:\n      containers:\n        - name: backend",
  "new_string": "    spec:\n      # Kubernetes has no depends_on: wait for Postgres so Flyway doesn't fail and crash-loop at startup.\n      initContainers:\n        - name: wait-for-postgres\n          image: postgres:16-alpine\n          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent\n          command: [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"until pg_isready -h postgres -p 5432 -q; do echo waiting for postgres; sleep 2; done\"]\n          resources:\n            requests:\n              cpu: 10m\n              memory: 16Mi\n            limits:\n              memory: 64Mi\n      containers:\n        - name: backend"
}

s=s.rstrip('\n')+"""

## Infrastructure

- **Verified on Docker Desktop 29 and kind 0.33.** `docker compose up --build` brought all three
  services up healthy on the first try; the Playwright suite and the Testcontainers-backed API tests
  pass against it. The same Playwright suite passes through the kind cluster.
- **The backend waits for Postgres in an init container.** The first kind run showed the backend
  starting before Postgres accepted connections, so Flyway failed and the pod restarted twice before
  settling. Compose avoids this with `depends_on: service_healthy`; Kubernetes has no equivalent, so a
  small `pg_isready` init container now gates startup. A cold start has zero restarts.
- **Pods pause five seconds before stopping.** One request right after a rollout hit nginx's upstream
  while the Service still routed to the old backend pod. A `preStop` sleep keeps a pod serving until the
  endpoint change has propagated, the usual fix for this rolling-update race.
- **Images are loaded, not pulled.** The manifests use `:local` tags with `IfNotPresent`, matching
  `kind load docker-image`. A real cluster would push versioned images to a registry instead.
"""
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF
tail -5 docs/DECISIONS.md

- **Images are loaded, not pulled.** The manifests use `:local` tags with `IfNotPresent`, matching

Yes, Docker is now part of the project. The Docker files were already in the repo but had never been run, and now they're tested end to end. `docker compose up --build` brought the database, backend and frontend up healthy on the first try, with no changes needed. The Compose stack is still running at http://localhost:8080. **What I ran:** - **Compose stack:** all 27 browser tests pass against it (Playwright, with the dev profile turned on for the run). Without it, the test-only endpoint correctly returns 404. - **Backend tests:** all 80 pass, with Testcontainers starting its own Postgres in Docker. I said 94 tests last time; that was a miscount. - **Kubernetes:** I installed `kind` with winget, as you chose, and deployed `k8s/` to a throwaway cluster. The same 27 browser tests pass through it. **Two Kubernetes fixes the first run turned up:** - **Startup order:** the backend started before Postgres was accepting connections, crashed and restarted twice before settling. It now waits for the database before starting, and a fresh deploy comes up with zero restarts. - **Rolling updates:** one request right after a backend update timed out while the old pod was shutting down. Pods now keep serving for five seconds on shutdown, which closes that gap. I updated the README with a verification section and Windows commands to use instead of `make`. It also notes that Compose and the Kubernetes port-forward both use port 8080, so stop one before starting the other. DECISIONS.md and TIME_LOG.md cover the fixes and this session, about 41 minutes. Everything is in commit `847fd20`. I deleted the test cluster to free Docker's memory; `kind` stays installed, so the README's Kubernetes steps recreate it in about a minute. If `kind` isn't found right away, open a new terminal so it picks up the updated PATH.

Mark them with data attributes:\n * - data-prop=\"hero\": a signature prop, checked to stay visible beside the board;\n * - data-crosser: something that crosses the scene now and then (removed while paused, so a frozen\n *   frame never shows it mid-flight, and it restarts off-screen);\n * - data-secondary: hidden on small screens, where only the hero remains.\n */\nexport function SceneFrame({ name, mode = 'full', animate, scrim = false, particles, children, props }: SceneFrameProps) {\n  return (\n    <div className={styles.scene} data-scene={name} data-mode={mode} data-animate={animate} data-scrim={scrim} aria-hidden=\"true\">\n      <div className={styles.photo} />\n      <div className={styles.layers}>{children}</div>\n      {props && <div className={styles.props}>{props}</div>}\n      {particles && <ParticleCanvas create={particles} animate={animate} className={styles.canvas} />}\n      {scrim && <div className={styles.scrim} />}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

  "content": ".scene {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  overflow: hidden;\n  pointer-events: none;\n  contain: strict;\n  /* Props size and place themselves in cqw/cqh, relative to the scene, not the viewport. */\n  container-type: size;\n  /* How far props keep from the right edge: clear of the side panel on wide game pages. */\n  --right-inset: 0px;\n}\n\n@media (min-width: 1100px) {\n  .scene[data-mode='full'] {\n    --right-inset: calc(var(--panel-w) + var(--space-4));\n  }\n}\n\n.layers,\n.props {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n}\n\n/* A licensed photo can be dropped in later by setting one variable. */\n.photo {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  background: var(--scene-photo, none) center / cover no-repeat;\n}\n\n.canvas {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  width: 100%;\n  height: 100%;\n}\n\n/* Scenes are always rendered; motion is opt-in. Paused keyframes still show a natural frame. */\n.scene:not([data-animate='true']) :global(*) {\n  animation-play-state: paused !important;\n}\n\n/* Crossers only exist while the scene moves, so they always restart off-screen. */\n.scene:not([data-animate='true']) [data-crosser] {\n  display: none;\n}\n\n@media (max-width: 599px) {\n  .scene [data-crosser],\n  .scene [data-secondary] {\n    display: none;\n  }\n}\n\n/* Behind a board the scene is a backdrop: desaturated, then darkened most behind the board. */\n.scene[data-scrim='true'] > .photo,\n.scene[data-scrim='true'] > .layers,\n.scene[data-scrim='true'] > .canvas {\n  filter: saturate(0.55);\n}\n\n/* Props are muted a little less so they don't turn muddy; the scrim still sits on top of them. */\n.scene[data-scrim='true'] > .props {\n  filter: saturate(0.8);\n}\n\n.scrim {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  background: radial-gradient(\n    ellipse 65% 70% at var(--scrim-x, 50%) 55%,\n    var(--ui-scrim) 0%,\n    color-mix(in srgb, var(--ui-scrim) 70%, transparent) 60%,\n    color-mix(in srgb, var(--ui-scrim) 40%, transparent) 100%\n  );\n}\n"
}

}

2. Key Technical Concepts:

   **Stack**
   - Java 21 (built locally with JBR 25 at `~/.jdks/jbr-25.0.4.1`, `export JAVA_HOME`) and Spring Boot 3.5.16, JPA, Flyway, PostgreSQL 16.
   - React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 6, CSS Modules, lucide-react.
   - Playwright run with `PW_CHANNEL=msedge`; Vitest.
   - Docker Compose, Kustomize/kind (kind 0.33 via winget, at `C:\Users\ustec\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links`), GitHub CLI at `C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe`.

   **Scene architecture**
   - SceneFrame layers: photo, `.layers` (saturate .55 under scrim), `.props` (saturate .8 under scrim), particle canvas, then scrim.
   - `.scene` is `container-type: size`, so props use cqw/cqh units (works full-page and in 280×336 card thumbnails).
   - `--right-inset` is `calc(var(--panel-w) + var(--space-4))` at min-width 1100px in `[data-mode='full']`, so props clear the side panel.
   - `[data-crosser]` gets `display:none` when not animating, so crossers restart off-screen.
   - Below 600px, `[data-crosser]` and `[data-secondary]` are hidden.
   - Animations pause via `.scene:not([data-animate='true']) :global(*) { animation-play-state: paused !important }`. The 0% keyframe must be the rest pose; no negative delays on animal actions.

   **Dev environment**
   - The compose stack runs at localhost:8080, currently with `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev`. Restore with `docker compose up -d --wait` without the env var at the end.
   - Vite dev server at 5173 (preview "frontend"; launch.json in .claude/), proxying /api to 8080.
   - The browser pane tab "seed" is localhost; tab-1 holds the user's PDF.

   ```tsx
   interface SceneFrameProps extends SceneProps { name: string; particles?: ParticleFactory; children: ReactNode;
     /** Animals and objects, on their own layer so the scrim can mute them less than the landscape. */
     props?: ReactNode; }
   export function SceneFrame({ name, mode = 'full', animate, scrim = false, particles, children, props }: SceneFrameProps) {
     return (
       <div className={styles.scene} data-scene={name} data-mode={mode} data-animate={animate} data-scrim={scrim} aria-hidden="true">
         <div className={styles.photo} />
         <div className={styles.layers}>{children}</div>
         {props && <div className={styles.props}>{props}</div>}
         {particles && <ParticleCanvas create={particles} animate={animate} className={styles.canvas} />}
         {scrim && <div className={styles.scrim} />}
       </div>);
   }
   ```

.page {
  position: relative;
  min-height: 100vh;
  min-height: 100dvh;
  background: var(--ui-bg);
}

/* The scene stays put behind the content, even when the cards scroll on a phone. */
.page > [data-scene] {
  position: fixed;
}

.settings {
  position: absolute;
  top: var(--space-3);
  right: var(--space-3);
  z-index: 2;
  color: var(--jg-cream);
  --ui-text: var(--jg-cream);
}

.main {
  position: relative;
  z-index: 1;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-6);
  padding: var(--space-7) var(--space-4) var(--space-6);
}

.header {
  text-align: center;
}

.wordmark {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: var(--text-2xl);
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  color: var(--jg-cream);
  line-height: 1.1;
}

.subtitle {
  margin-top: var(--space-2);
  color: rgba(244, 241, 232, 0.82);
  font-size: var(--text-md);
}

.cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 280px));
  gap: var(--space-6);
  justify-content: center;
  width: 100%;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

  "content": "// Usage: node at.cjs <route> <WxH> <name> <class-fragment>=<seconds> [...]\n// Seeks the named elements' CSS animations to a time, pauses everything, and screenshots.\nconst { createRequire } = require('module');\nconst path = require('path');\nconst req = createRequire('C:/Users/ustec/Downloads/Chess_Project/frontend/package.json');\nconst { chromium } = req('@playwright/test');\n(async () => {\n  const [route, size, name, ...seeks] = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const [width, height] = size.split('x').map(Number);\n  const browser = await chromium.launch({ channel: 'msedge' });\n  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } });\n  await page.goto('http://localhost:5173' + route);\n  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);\n  const report = await page.evaluate((seeks) => {\n    const out = [];\n    for (const s of seeks) {\n      const [frag, sec] = s.split('=');\n      const els = [...document.querySelectorAll(`[class*=\"${frag}\"]`)];\n      for (const el of els) {\n        for (const a of el.getAnimations()) {\n          a.currentTime = Number(sec) * 1000;\n          a.pause();\n        }\n        const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n        out.push(`${frag}: ${Math.round(r.x)},${Math.round(r.y)} ${Math.round(r.width)}x${Math.round(r.height)}`);\n      }\n    }\n    return out;\n  }, seeks);\n  console.log(report.join('\\n'));\n  await page.waitForTimeout(200);\n  const out = path.join(__dirname, 'shots', `${name}.png`);\n  await page.screenshot({ path: out });\n  console.log(out);\n  await browser.close();\n})();\n"
}

Claude’s reasoning
The checkerboard uses white and navy, so the winter props will use snow whites and pine blues to avoid clashing. I'm building a shared tiered-pine helper first, so the far pines, near pines and gutter pines all get snow caps with blue shadows.

{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\frontend\\src\\themes\\winter\\pine.ts",
  "content": "/** Flat SVG paths for one pine: the tree, the snow caps, and the blue shadow on each cap's far side. */\nexport interface PinePaths {\n  tree: string;\n  snow: string;\n  shade: string;\n}\n\nconst r = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 10) / 10;\n\n/**\n * A pine of `tiers` stacked tiers whose base is centred on (x, y), `h` tall and `w` wide at the bottom.\n * Each tier carries a snow cap with a soft scalloped edge; `depth` is how far down the tier the snow\n * reaches (0.5 for a dusting, 0.65 for heavily laden). Light comes from the left, so the right half of\n * every cap is in blue shadow.\n */\nexport function pine(x: number, y: number, h: number, w: number, tiers = 3, depth = 0.5): PinePaths {\n  const th = (1.27 * h) / tiers;\n  const tree: string[] = [];\n  const snow: string[] = [];\n  const shade: string[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < tiers; i++) {\n    const t = tiers === 1 ? 1 : i / (tiers - 1);\n    const top = y - h + (i * (h - th)) / Math.max(1, tiers - 1);\n    const bottom = top + th;\n    const topW = w * 0.1 * t;\n    const halfW = w * (0.24 + 0.26 * t);\n    tree.push(\n      `M${r(x - topW)} ${r(top)} L${r(x + topW)} ${r(top)} L${r(x + halfW)} ${r(bottom)} Q${r(x)} ${r(bottom + h * 0.035)} ${r(x - halfW)} ${r(bottom)} Z`,\n    );\n\n    const capY = top + th * depth;\n    const capW = (topW + (halfW - topW) * depth) * 1.08;\n    const d = th * 0.12;\n    const edge = `L${r(x + capW)} ${r(capY)} Q${r(x + capW * 0.55)} ${r(capY + d * 1.6)} ${r(x + capW * 0.1)} ${r(capY + d * 0.2)}`;\n    snow.push(\n      `M${r(x - topW * 1.1)} ${r(top - 1)} L${r(x + topW * 1.1)} ${r(top - 1)} ${edge} Q${r(x - capW * 0.4)} ${r(capY + d * 1.8)} ${r(x - capW)} ${r(capY)} Z`,\n    );\n    shade.push(`M${r(x)} ${r(top - 1)} L${r(x + topW * 1.1)} ${r(top - 1)} ${edge} Z`);\n  }\n  return { tree: tree.join(' '), snow: snow.join(' '), shade: shade.join(' ') };\n}\n\n/** A row of snow-capped pines along a baseline, spread across a 1600-wide drawing. */\nexport function pineRow(baseline: number, count: number, height: number, seed: number): PinePaths {\n  const rows: PinePaths[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n    const jitter = Math.sin(seed + i * 12.9898) * 0.5 + 0.5;\n    const x = (i + 0.2 + jitter * 0.6) * (1600 / count);\n    const h = height * (0.7 + jitter * 0.5);\n    rows.push(pine(x, baseline + jitter * 10, h, h * 0.42));\n  }\n  return {\n    tree: rows.map((p) => p.tree).join(' '),\n    snow: rows.map((p) => p.snow).join(' '),\n    shade: rows.map((p) => p.shade).join(' '),\n  };\n}\n"
}

.scene {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  pointer-events: none;
  contain: strict;
  /* Props size and place themselves in cqw/cqh, relative to the scene, not the viewport. */
  container-type: size;
  /* How far props keep from the right edge: clear of the side panel on wide game pages. */
  --right-inset: 0px;
}

@media (min-width: 1100px) {
  .scene[data-mode='full'] {
    --right-inset: calc(var(--panel-w) + var(--space-4));
  }
}

.layers,
.props {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
}

/* A licensed photo can be dropped in later by setting one variable. */
.photo {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background: var(--scene-photo, none) center / cover no-repeat;
}

.canvas {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
}

{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\frontend\\src\\themes\\winter\\Cabin.module.css",
  "content": "/* In the gap between the board and the side panel, low down among the near pines. */\n.cabin {\n  position: absolute;\n  right: calc(var(--right-inset) + 2cqw);\n  bottom: 7cqh;\n  width: clamp(70px, 6.5cqw, 120px);\n}\n\n.cabin svg {\n  display: block;\n  width: 100%;\n  height: auto;\n  overflow: visible;\n}\n\n.log {\n  fill: #6b4a36;\n}\n\n.logDark {\n  fill: #5a3d2c;\n}\n\n.roof,\n.door {\n  fill: #4a3527;\n}\n\n.stone {\n  fill: #4d4a52;\n}\n\n.snow {\n  fill: #eef3f8;\n}\n\n.snowShade {\n  fill: #b9cbe0;\n}\n\n/* The lamp-lit window: the theme's warm accent, flickering only slightly. */\n.window {\n  fill: #f2c48d;\n  animation: flicker 3.7s ease-in-out infinite;\n}\n\n.puff {\n  fill: #c9d4e3;\n  opacity: 0;\n  transform-box: fill-box;\n  transform-origin: center;\n  animation: smoke 7.9s ease-out infinite both;\n}\n\n.puffB {\n  animation-delay: 2.6s;\n}\n\n.puffC {\n  animation-delay: 5.2s;\n}\n\n@keyframes flicker {\n  0%,\n  100% {\n    opacity: 1;\n  }\n  31% {\n    opacity: 0.88;\n  }\n  37% {\n    opacity: 0.97;\n  }\n  64% {\n    opacity: 0.9;\n  }\n}\n\n/* Each puff rises, drifts right, swells and fades: a slow curl from the chimney. */\n@keyframes smoke {\n  0% {\n    opacity: 0;\n    transform: translate(0, 0) scale(0.6);\n  }\n  15% {\n    opacity: 0.6;\n  }\n  55% {\n    transform: translate(6px, -14px) scale(1.2);\n  }\n  100% {\n    opacity: 0;\n    transform: translate(2px, -30px) scale(1.8);\n  }\n}\n\n[data-mode='thumbnail'] .cabin {\n  display: none;\n}\n"
}

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { subscribe } from './ticker';

/** A particle system drawn in CSS pixels. Created per canvas size; stepped by the shared ticker. */
export interface ParticleField {
  update(dt: number, now: number): void;
  draw(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D): void;
}

/**
 * @param scale particle-count multiplier: 1 at 1440×900, less on small screens
 */
export type ParticleFactory = (width: number, height: number, scale: number) => ParticleField;

interface ParticleCanvasProps {
  create: ParticleFactory;
  animate: boolean;
  className?: string;
}

const REFERENCE_AREA = 1440 * 900;

export function ParticleCanvas({ create, animate, className }: ParticleCanvasProps) {
  const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const canvas = canvasRef.current;
    const ctx = canvas?.getContext('2d');
    if (!canvas || !ctx) return;

    let field: ParticleField | null = null;
    let width = 0;
    let height = 0;

    function render() {
      if (!ctx || !field) return;
      const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
      ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);
      field.draw(ctx);
    }

    function resize() {
      if (!canvas) return;
      const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;
      width = rect.width;
      height = rect.heigh

  x: number;

  width: number;

async function cellRects(page: Page): Promise<Rect[]> {
  return page.locator('[data-testid="board"] [data-cell]').evaluateAll((cells) =>
    cells.map((cell) => {
      const r = cell.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { x: r.x, y: r.y, width: r.width, height: r.height };
    }),
  );
}

  });
}

  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\ustec\\Downloads\\Chess_Project\\frontend\\e2e\\scenes.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { expect, test, type Page } from '@playwright/test';\nimport { GAMES, waitForHumanTurn } from './games';\n\n// Hero props (data-prop=\"hero\") must stay at least half visible: inside the viewport and not hidden\n// behind the board, the side panel, the top bar, or on the home page the cards and the title.\nconst VIEWPORTS = [\n  { width: 1440, height: 900 },\n  { width: 1920, height: 1080 },\n];\nconst TOP_BAR = 56;\nconst GRID = 12;\n\ninterface Rect {\n  x: number;\n  y: number;\n  width: number;\n  height: number;\n}\n\n/** For each hero in the full-page scene: its name and the share of a sample grid that is unobstructed. */\nasync function heroVisibility(page: Page, blockers: string[], topBar: number) {\n  return page.evaluate(\n    ({ blockers, topBar, grid }) => {\n      const rects: Rect[] = blockers.flatMap((selector) =>\n        [...document.querySelectorAll(selector)].map((el) => el.getBoundingClientRect()),\n      );\n      const blocked = (x: number, y: number) =>\n        x < 0 ||\n        y < topBar ||\n        x > window.innerWidth ||\n        y > window.innerHeight ||\n        rects.some((r) => x >= r.x && x <= r.x + r.width && y >= r.y && y <= r.y + r.height);\n      return [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-scene][data-mode=\"full\"] [data-prop=\"hero\"]')].map((hero) => {\n        const r = hero.getBoundingClientRect();\n        let clear = 0;\n        for (let i = 0; i < grid; i++) {\n          for (let j = 0; j < grid; j++) {\n            if (!blocked(r.x + (r.width * (i + 0.5)) / grid, r.y + (r.height * (j + 0.5)) / grid)) clear++;\n          }\n        }\n        return { name: String(hero.className), visible: clear / (grid * grid), width: r.width };\n      });\n    },\n    { blockers, topBar, grid: GRID },\n  );\n}\n\nfor (const viewport of VIEWPORTS) {\n  for (const game of GAMES) {\n    test(`${game.name} scene heroes are visible at ${viewport.width}×${viewport.height}`, async ({ page }) => {\n      await page.setViewportSize(viewport);\n      await page.goto(game.path);\n      await waitForHumanTurn(page);\n\n      const heroes = await heroVisibility(page, ['[data-testid=\"board\"]', '[data-testid=\"panel\"]'], TOP_BAR);\n      expect(heroes.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n      for (const hero of heroes) {\n        expect(hero.width, hero.name).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n        expect(hero.visible, hero.name).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.5);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  test(`home scene heroes are visible at ${viewport.width}×${viewport.height}`, async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.setViewportSize(viewport);\n    await page.goto('/');\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();\n\n    const heroes = await heroVisibility(page, ['main header', 'main li'], 0);\n    expect(heroes.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n    for (const hero of heroes) {\n      expect(hero.width, hero.name).toBeGreaterThan(0);\n      expect(hero.visible, hero.name).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.5);\n    }\n  });\n}\n"
}

  which is close to optimal there.
- **Checkers have identities on the client.** Each checker gets an id from a base position, replayed
  through the steps since then, so moves, hits (to the bar) and bear-offs (to the tray) all slide.
  Stacks over five show a count badge instead of overflowing the point.

## Polish

- **Ambient motion follows the system until the player chooses.** The setting is only saved once it is
  toggled, so a later `prefers-reduced-motion` change still applies to anyone who never touched it.
- **Accessibility is tested, not just intended.** A Playwright spec drives Connect Four and Checkers
  entirely from the keyboard, checks the result modal traps focus and returns it, opens a game from
  the home page with Tab and Enter, and confirms every scene is static under reduced motion.
- **Contrast was measured.** All text/surface pairs in the four themes clear WCAG AA (most are 8:1 or
  better). The home page's lagoon teal was deepened from #2F8F86 to #287A72 so white button text
  reaches 5.1:1.

## Scene refresh

A design-only pass on the four ambient scenes, from a second brief; game logic, the API, boards and
panel are untouched.

- **What was added.** Home is now a rainforest: a dark canopy band with small light gaps, misty far
  trunks, warm light shafts, a three-tier waterfall into a pool, buttressed trunks with lianas, and
  two-tone ferns, monstera, fan palm and heliconia. A toucan, a hanging monkey, a sloth and a snake sit
  around the edges, and a parrot crosses the canopy about once a minute. The ocean gained a sandy seabed
  with shells and a starfish, a half-buried treasure chest, a seahorse on its own kelp stem, a fish
  school, two reef fish, coral and an anemone. In winter every pine tier, near and far, carries a snow
  cap with a blue shadow side, and the scene has two heavily snowed pines that shed a clump of snow, a
  frozen lake, and an arctic fox curled on the bank. The desert has a saguaro, a half-sunk cow skull, a
  prickly pear with one flower, a hazy mesa with two far saguaros, and a tumbleweed.
- **One biome per scene.** Every animal on the home page is Central or South American. The brief's
  green tree python is from New Guinea, so the snake is drawn as an emerald tree boa, the Amazon's
  near-identical look-alike. The ocean is a generic tropical reef (no named species, no clownfish
  stripes). Winter is boreal, so no penguins. The desert is the American Southwest: no camels or
  pyramids.
- **Props get their own layer.** Behind a board the landscape is desaturated to 0.55. The animals and
  objects sit on a separate layer at 0.8, so they don't turn muddy, and the scrim still covers both.
  Where a prop meets the ground (the chest's sand, the skull's sand) its colours are pre-muted to match
  the landscape layer, so it sinks in rather than sitting on top.
- **Heroes live in the gutters and are tested there.** Props size and place themselves in container
  units, so the same scene works full-page and in a 280px card. On wide screens a shared `--gutter-mid`
  centres heroes in the left gutter rather than pinning them to the dark scrimmed edge. A Playwright
  spec checks that every hero is at least half visible, clear of the board, panel and top bar (cards
  and title on the home page), at 1440 × 900 and 1920 × 1080.
- **Motion stays CSS.** Every animation is a keyframe on transform or opacity, and its first frame is
  the resting pose, so the paused scene looks natural. Crossers (parrot, fish school, tumbleweed) are
  hidden while paused, so they restart off-screen. The tumbleweed's sand gust reuses the existing
  particle canvas: factories now get their canvas, and the desert field reads the tumbleweed's own CSS
  animation clock instead of running a second timer.
- **Cut or swapped, and why.**
  - The bottom-right heliconia was removed because it hid the snake.
  - The light gaps in the canopy were first drawn as bright discs, which read as lamps. They became
    small lime leaf clusters.

  - The toucan moved below the canopy, where it had been invisible against the dark leaves.

Claude Nov 05, 03:34 UTC
I've finished the scene refresh and pushed it to `origin main`; the last commit is **2ecb26e**. All the tests pass:

- **Backend:** 80 of 80.
- **Vitest:** 26 of 26.
- **Playwright:** 35 of 35, including 8 new checks that each hero stays at least half visible at 1440×900 and 1920×1080. I confirmed the check catches a hero moved onto the board.
- **Screenshots:** 17 of 17 regenerated, plus three new shots of home with each card hovered. I opened every one.

The moodboard is git-ignored and appears nowhere in the history.

## What each scene got
Screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/`.

- **Home** (`home-*.png`, `home-1440x900-hover-*.png`): it's now a bright rainforest.
  - Dark canopy band with small light gaps, misty far trunks, warm light shafts.
  - A three-tier waterfall into a pool, big trunks with roots, moss and swaying vines.
  - Ferns, monstera, fan palm and heliconia.
  - Animals:
    - Toucan: head tilt and blink.
    - Parrot: flies across the canopy about once a minute.
    - Monkey: hangs from its vine, swings ±4° and looks around.
    - Sloth: blinks and turns its head.
    - Snake: breathing ripple and tongue flick.
  - Fixing the canopy also fixed the subtitle: it now sits on solid dark green at about 9:1 contrast.
- **Connect Four ocean** (`connect-four-*.png`):
  - Sandy seabed with shells and a starfish.
  - Half-buried chest (rim glint, bubbles).
  - Seahorse on its own kelp stem (bob, fin flutter).
  - A fish school crossing every ~31s, two reef fish that swim back and forth, coral and a swaying anemone.
  - Manta, light rays and bubbles are kept.
- **Checkers winter** (`checkers-*.png`):
  - Every pine tier, near and far, has a snow cap with a blue shadow side.
  - Two heavily snowed pines that drop a clump of snow with a puff every ~24s.
  - A frozen lake with reflections, cracks and a glint sweep every ~12s.
  - An arctic fox curled on the bank: tail swish, ear twitch, slow blink, looks up about once a minute, paw prints.
- **Backgammon desert** (`backgammon-*.png`):
  - A saguaro and a half-sunk cow skull in the narrow left gutter.
  - A prickly pear with one pink flower, a hazy mesa and two small far saguaros.
  - A tumbleweed rolls along the bottom every ~32s, and the sand gust fires as it sets off.

## Cut or swapped, and why
- **Snake:** a green tree python is from New Guinea and everything else on the home page is Central/South American. I drew it as an emerald tree boa, which looks almost identical.
- **Home redraws:**
  - The first canopy gaps read as lamps; they're now small leaf clusters.
  - The waterfall's stacked boulders looked like pillars; it's now a stepped cliff.
  - The bottom-right heliconia hid the snake, so I removed it.
- **Fox:** the first version read as a mouse, so it got a bushier tail and a shorter muzzle.
- **Left out to stay within about five new elements per page:** the boardwalk, butterflies and frog, the jellyfish, the wolf, and the lizard and hawk.
- **Log cabin:** this optional one is in its own commit (67281e4), so it's easy to drop.

## Things you may want to look at
- **Gutter centring:** on wide screens the heroes hugged the dark left edge, so a new shared `--gutter-mid` value centres them in the gutter. It assumes the board's maximum width, so it never puts a hero over the board.
- **Tumbleweed gust:** to time the sand gust to the tumbleweed, sand systems now receive their own canvas. That's a one-line change in the shared particle code, not a new loop.
- **Phones:** the board and cards fill the width, so each page's one remaining hero mostly sits behind them. The phone card thumbnails still show both heroes.
- **Extra commits beyond the brief's list:** the hero check, the phone-thumbnail fix and the docs.

The Docker stack is back on the default profile, and the browser preview is back to its normal size.

The cause was my cleanup step, not the README. That link just opens whatever your local Docker stack is serving. After the tests, I put the stack back on its normal settings with `docker compose up -d --wait`, which restarts the existing containers but doesn't rebuild them. So the frontend kept running the build from 20:30, before the scene refresh. I've now run `docker compose up --build -d --wait`, and the frontend container is rebuilt and healthy.

Your guess about "needs Docker with Compose" was close, but that line is only the prerequisite. The README's commands already include `--build`, and `make up` rebuilds too, so I didn't change any files. In future, any start command with `--build` (or `make up`) will pick up new code; a plain `docker compose up -d` won't.

    listen 80;

    gzip on;
    gzip_types application/json text/css application/javascript image/svg+xml;

    location /api/ {

Claude Nov 05, 03:47 UTC
This is fixed on your machine. Clicking the localhost link now opens the new version on the first try.

**Why it happened:** the Docker frontend served the main page with a "last modified" date but no instruction on how long to keep it. So your browser kept its own saved copy of the old page and opened that when you followed a link. A reload makes the browser check with the server, which is why the second load was right.

**The fix:** one line in `frontend/nginx.conf`. It tells browsers to check with the server every time they open the page. When nothing has changed, the server answers with a tiny "not modified" reply, so it's no slower. The build's other files keep their year-long caching, which is safe because their names change with every build. I also added a line to `docs/DECISIONS.md` explaining why.

**Checked:**
- I rebuilt the stack and confirmed the main page and game pages now carry that "always check" instruction.
- In a real browser I opened the app, left it, then followed a plain link back twice, like clicking it on GitHub. The server saw every visit, so a new build shows on the first click.

The fix isn't committed yet.
